title: Where Is the Land of Opportunity? The Geography of Intergenerational Mobility in the United States
method: US administrative income data; geographic comparisons
takeaway: Economic mobility differs strikingly across US regions, motivating a closer look at the places and institutions that shape opportunity.
description: A foundational mapping of geographic variation in US intergenerational mobility using linked parent-child income records.

title: The Role of Bequests in Shaping Wealth Inequality: Evidence from Danish Wealth Records
method: Danish administrative wealth records; parental death event study
takeaway: Bequests can raise absolute wealth dispersion while reducing relative measures of inequality — a reminder that inequality metrics matter.
description: Studies wealth distributions before and after parental death in Danish administrative records.

title: Intergenerational Wealth Mobility and the Role of Inheritance: Evidence from Multiple Generations
method: Swedish multigenerational wealth and inheritance records
takeaway: Transfers and bequests help explain the persistence of wealth across several generations.
description: Links wealth and inheritance data across up to four generations to quantify persistence and channels of transmission.

title: The Effects of Exposure to Better Neighborhoods on Children: New Evidence from the Moving to Opportunity Experiment
method: Randomized housing voucher experiment linked to tax records
takeaway: Moving to lower-poverty neighborhoods benefits young children in adulthood, highlighting the importance of childhood exposure.
description: Revisits the Moving to Opportunity experiment to study long-run outcomes by children’s age at relocation.

title: The More the Merrier? The Effect of Family Size and Birth Order on Children’s Education
method: Norwegian population registers; twin births and birth-order comparisons
takeaway: Birth order appears more consequential for educational outcomes than family size once key confounders are addressed.
description: Uses Norwegian register data to distinguish the roles of family size and birth order in children’s educational attainment.

title: Yours, Mine, and Ours: Do Divorce Laws Affect the Intertemporal Behavior of Married Couples?
method: Changes in US divorce laws; household decision model
takeaway: Property division rules alter saving and labor decisions within marriage, linking family institutions to resource allocation.
description: Analyzes how changes in divorce and property-division laws affect household intertemporal choices.

title: The Impacts of Neighborhoods on Intergenerational Mobility I: Childhood Exposure Effects
method: Mover design; sibling comparisons; linked administrative data
takeaway: Children gain more from moving to better neighborhoods when exposure occurs earlier, consistent with cumulative childhood effects.
description: Uses the timing of family moves across areas to estimate childhood exposure effects of place.

title: The Impacts of Neighborhoods on Intergenerational Mobility II: County-Level Estimates
takeaway: Where a child grows up matters, with substantial variation in estimated opportunity even within metro areas.
description: Estimates causal county effects on adult income using linked data and variation in the timing of childhood moves.

title: From the Cradle to the Labor Market? The Effect of Birth Weight on Adult Outcomes
takeaway: Early-life health differences can affect education and adult labor-market outcomes, providing one route from childhood conditions to inequality.
description: Studies the long-run consequences of birth weight using linked Norwegian population records and twin comparisons.

title: Mobility Report Cards: The Role of Colleges in Intergenerational Mobility
method: US tax and higher-education administrative data; descriptive mobility measures
takeaway: Colleges differ greatly in low-income access and mobility outcomes, showing how institutional access can reproduce or reduce advantage.
description: Documents intergenerational income mobility by college using large-scale US administrative data.

title: Born with a Silver Spoon? Danish Evidence on Wealth Inequality in Childhood
method: Danish wealth records; descriptive childhood wealth distributions
takeaway: Wealth inequality emerges already in childhood, and wealth at age 18 predicts later outcomes beyond parental wealth alone.
description: Examines childhood assets and the role of inter vivos transfers in Danish register data.

title: Parenting with Style: Altruism and Paternalism in Intergenerational Preference Transmission
method: Theoretical model of parenting and preference transmission
takeaway: A model of how socioeconomic conditions shape parenting strategies and thereby influence the transmission of preferences.
description: Develops a theory of parenting styles in which parents combine altruism and paternalism.
